title: Artificial Intelligence‒Guided Phenotyping of Cardiomyopathies: From Detection to Surveillance.
authors: Evangelos K Oikonomou; Rohan Khera; Ahmad Masri
abstract: The management of cardiomyopathies relies on timely diagnosis, precise phenotyping, multimodal risk stratification, and longitudinal monitoring. These tasks require integration of high-dimensional signals from patient history, electrocardiography, imaging, biomarkers, and longitudinal health records, data streams well-suited to artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled pattern recognition and prediction. Among inherited and acquired cardiomyopathies, hypertrophic (HCM) and transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) best exemplify this opportunity. Both remain systematically underdiagnosed, span a continuous phenotypic spectrum, and are increasingly actionable through disease-modifying therapies. Emerging AI approaches applied to multimodality data streams can identify latent disease, quantify its severity, and predict its trajectory. Beyond diagnosis, AI paves the path for opportunistic screening, longitudinal surveillance, risk stratification, and novel clinical trial designs. Realizing this promise requires careful attention to label quality, generalizability, false-positive burden in low-prevalence settings, and prospective evidence that the human-AI synergy improves outcomes. In this review, we use HCM and ATTR-CM as key examples to synthesize the current evidence of AI in cardiomyopathies and propose a forward-looking framework for AI-guided disease phenotyping, with emphasis on regulation, implementation, and clinical evaluation.

title: Routine Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Versus Conservative Management in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
authors: Ahmed Adel Mohamed; Bandar Alawlaqi; Abdullah Moemen Ahmed; Ahmed Elhadi; Ali Samir Galal; Eslam Saber Mahmoud; Ibrahim Saeed Shahda; Habiba Mostafa; Kenzy Ahmed Mohammed; Yousef Abdul-Rafea Saad; Hamzah M Alghzawi
abstract: Coronary artery disease commonly coexists with severe aortic stenosis in transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) candidates, yet optimal revascularization remains debated. We meta-analyzed randomized controlled trials comparing routine percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) before or concomitant with TAVI versus conservative management. Major databases were searched through May 2026. Random-effects models calculated risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and evidence certainty was evaluated via the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation. Three randomized controlled trials (1156 patients; PCI: n = 579, conservative: n = 577) were included. Routine PCI was not associated with significant reductions in all-cause mortality (RR, 0.90; 95% CI, 0.70-1.15; P = 0.40), cardiac death (RR, 0.74; 95% CI, 0.51-1.08; P = 0.12), myocardial infarction (RR, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.45-1.64; P = 0.64), stroke (RR, 0.70; 95% CI, 0.48-1.03; P = 0.07), or hospitalization (RR, 1.07; 95% CI, 0.87-1.32; P = 0.52). However, PCI significantly increased major bleeding (RR, 1.57; 95% CI, 1.06-2.34; P = 0.02) and any bleeding (RR, 1.77; 95% CI, 1.27-2.48; P = 0.0008), while reducing urgent and repeat revascularization. In conclusion, routine PCI before or concomitant with TAVI reduces subsequent revascularization without conferring survival or ischemic benefit, while increasing bleeding complications. Given the moderate-to-low certainty of evidence, limited cumulative sample size, and clinical heterogeneity across trials, these findings warrant cautious interpretation and favor an individualized, Heart Team-guided revascularization strategy over routine PCI.

title: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation with Vitaflow prosthesis in Latin America.
authors: Juan G Chiabrando; Verónica González; Alfredo Rodríguez; Germán Cafaro; Marcelo Menéndez; José Lazarte; Agustín Hauqui; Oscar Mendiz; Pablo Lamelas; Matías Sztejfman
abstract:
Robust long-term data on the performance and durability of novel transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) valve designs, especially in Latin America, are lacking and warrant further investigation.
To provide a 1 year follow-up data regarding a novel TAVI device.
A retrospective, multicenter cohort study was conducted in Latin America of patients with severe symptomatic aortic stenosis treated with the Vitaflow prosthesis from June 2022 to June 2023. The clinical endpoints were all-cause death, cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, vascular and bleeding complications, permanent pacemaker implantation (PPM), and heart failure admission. Echocardiographic outcomes were the transvalvular gradient and paravalvular leak at 1 year of follow-up.
A total of 46 consecutive patients were included. The mean age of the patients was 80.9 ± 6.13 years; 50% were men, the mean STS score was 4.64 ± 2.67, and 60.8% were in NYHA class III/IV. The most used valve size was the 27 mm (47.1%). All-cause death at 1-year follow-up occurred in 4 patients (8.7%), of which 3 were cardiovascular (6.5%). There were 2 strokes, 1 vascular event, 2 major bleeding events, 4 new PPMs, and no myocardial infarctions or heart failure admissions. The 1-year mean transvalvular gradient was 7 ± 4 mmHg, and 3 patients (6.4%) had moderate paravalvular leak, with no severe leaks.
In a Latin American population, the Vitaflow TAVI valve has proved good safety and efficacy outcomes at 12 months of follow-up in the treatment of patients with severe aortic stenosis.

title: TAVR in anomalous origin of the right coronary artery with interarterial course and acute takeoff angle.
authors: José M Alanís-Naranjo; Oscar M Granados-Casas; Cielmar Galeana-Abarca; Julio C Mayen-Casas; Kevin D Aragón-Ontiveros; Arturo E Gudiño-Resendez; Alejandro Alcocer-Chauvet
abstract: Anomalous aortic origin of the coronary arteries (AAOCA) is an infrequent finding that may increase the risk of coronary obstruction during transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). We report the case of an 80-year-old woman with severe aortic stenosis and anomalous origin of the right coronary artery (RCA) from the left coronary sinus, with an interarterial course and an acute takeoff angle. Preprocedural coronary angiography showed ostioproximal occlusion. Intravascular ultrasound demonstrated approximately 80% extrinsic compression, and coronary physiologic assessment confirmed hemodynamically significant ischemia. Given the high risk of myocardial ischemia during TAVR, the RCA was treated with drug-eluting stents before valve implantation. Subsequently, transfemoral TAVR with a self-expandable valve was performed successfully, with preserved coronary patency and no complications. At 4-year follow-up, the patient remained asymptomatic, with a normally functioning prosthetic valve and no hospital readmissions. This case underscores the importance of detailed preprocedural imaging, coronary physiology assessment, and individualized planning to minimize the risk of coronary obstruction in patients with high-risk AAOCA undergoing TAVR.

title: Fluid-structure interaction simulation and analysis of the aortic valve under the condition of subaortic stenosis complicated with ascending aortic dilatation.
authors: Xiaoyang Xu; Fan Su
journal: Computer methods in biomechanics and biomedical engineering
abstract: Subaortic stenosis (SAS) and ascending aortic dilatation (AAD) often coexist, and the transitional stage from normal to early lesions is critical for intervention, yet their synergistic effects on the tricuspid aortic valve (TAV) remain unclear. This study used a standardized 3D fluid-structure interaction model to simulate nine cases combining different transvalvular gradients and ascending aortic diameters, in order to analyze leaflet kinematics and hemodynamics. The results showed significant synergistic amplification of flow velocity and wall shear stress (WSS). In severe combined lesions, peak flow velocity increased by 144.8% and peak WSS exceeded the physiological threshold by 42%, leading to premature over-opening and asymmetric leaflet motion. A high-risk reference range was identified: ascending aortic diameter ≥30 mm with transvalvular gradient ≥22 mmHg. These findings reveal the mechanical injury mechanism of early combined lesions and provide theoretical references for risk screening and individualized intervention in SAS-AAD patients.

title: Interleukin-6, soluble interleukin-6 receptor, and outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation: an exploratory biomarker substudy of a prospective multicenter cohort.
authors: Grzegorz Procyk; Paweł Tyrna; Izabela Młynarczuk-Biały; Jan Budzianowski; Anna Olasińska-Wiśniewska; Janusz Kochman; Aleksandra Gąsecka
abstract:
Severe aortic stenosis can be treated with transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). Identifying clinical and laboratory factors that predict clinical outcomes after TAVI may facilitate more informed decision-making. We aimed to assess the incidence of major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) within 12 months after TAVI and long-term survival according to baseline interleukin-6 (IL-6) and soluble interleukin-6 receptor (sIL-6R) levels.
In this biomarker substudy of a prospective multicenter cohort, we evaluated clinical outcomes after TAVI according to baseline IL-6 signal and sIL-6R concentration. We included only patients with an available baseline stored plasma sample. Patients were stratified into high and low IL-6 and sIL-6R groups. Two primary end points were analyzed: (i) 12-month MACCE, and (ii) long-term overall survival. Secondary end points included the individual components of MACCE. Stored baseline plasma was available for measurements in 62 patients who underwent TAVI between December 2018 and September 2021 across three clinical sites. Patients with high IL-6 had a higher 12-month MACCE risk in age- and sex-adjusted Firth penalized Cox regression analysis (HR 3.31; 95%CI 1.02-11.04, P = 0.0458) but not in unadjusted analysis (log-rank P = 0.07). The association was not robust to alternative cutoffs and the age- and sex-adjusted continuous analysis of IL-6 also did not show a statistically significant association (hazard ratio per 1-SD increase, 1.52, 95% CI, 0.86 to 2.46, P = 0.13). No significant associations were observed in the primary models between IL-6 and long-term overall survival or between sIL-6R and either primary end point.
High IL-6 signal at baseline may be associated with increased 12-month MACCE risk after TAVI, although this finding was sensitive to IL-6 categorization and was not statistically significant in continuous analysis. Baseline sIL-6R concentration was not significantly associated with the analyzed clinical outcomes. These findings should be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating.

title: Immediate and long-term outcomes of aortic commissurotomy for severe congenital aortic valve stenosis in infants: a single-center experience.
authors: Marek Rączka; Jacek Kuźma; Andrzej Rudziński; Piotr Weryński; Jacek Kołcz; Tomasz Mroczek; Janusz Skalski; Aleksandra Morka
journal: Kardiochirurgia i torakochirurgia polska = Polish journal of cardio-thoracic surgery
abstract:
Severe congenital aortic valve stenosis (AVS) in infants constitutes a significant therapeutic challenge. Currently, two methods are mostly used as first-line therapy: balloon aortic valvuloplasty (BAV) and surgical aortic valvotomy (SAV). In critically ill neonates, BAV is preferred as a less invasive procedure. If BAV fails, SAV remains an indispensable option.
To evaluate retrospectively the immediate and long-term outcomes of SAV as a primary procedure or re-intervention (after BAV) in infants with severe AVS.
SAV results were retrospectively analyzed in 23 children (including 3 born prematurely), operated on in the first year of life. Patients were divided into two groups: Gr-I (n = 9) infants with prior BAV and Gr-II (n = 14) infants who underwent SAV as the primary intervention. BAV was performed at a median age of 4 days, while SAV was performed at a median age of 50 days in Gr-I and 33 days in Gr-II. The mean follow-up period was 12.3 years.
Postoperative echocardiography showed a reduction in transvalvular pressure gradient (TVPG) and an increase in left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) in both groups. During hospitalization 10 (43.5%) infants developed various complications, which occurred more frequently in Gr-I. After SAV, 4 children (all from Gr-II) required 5 various re-interventions. One patient (Gr-I) died due to septicemia. In follow-up, 22 children were doing well and remained under outpatient supervision.
SAV as the first-line treatment or re-treatment after BAV in infants with severe AVS was associated with satisfactory outcomes. Both methods may complement each other, potentially delaying definitive aortic valve replacement.

title: From Valve to Spine and Spleen: Multisystem Complications of Gemella haemolysans Prosthetic-Valve Endocarditis.
authors: Eric Baghdasaryan; Sari Lada; Rafi Orphali; Ronak Jayswal; Sujay Dutta
abstract: Gemella haemolysans is an uncommon cause of infective endocarditis, yet infection involving a prosthetic valve may be accompanied by extensive extracardiac disease. A 79-year-old man with a history of transcatheter aortic valve replacement presented with fever, rigors, dyspnea, severe low back pain, and inability to walk after a fall. Two sets of blood cultures grew G. haemolysans. Echocardiography demonstrated a 0.6 × 0.6 cm vegetation at the aortic valve annulus. Lumbar magnetic resonance imaging identified discitis and vertebral osteomyelitis at L4-L5 and L5-S1, an anterior epidural abscess, and moderate-to-severe spinal canal stenosis. Abdominal imaging revealed a right psoas abscess and a 6.2-cm splenic infarction. Antimicrobial therapy was narrowed to intravenous ceftriaxone according to susceptibility testing. Fever resolved and inflammatory markers declined during hospitalization; a 6-week course was arranged at discharge without valve surgery. This case highlights the association between endocarditis and vertebral infection, the limitations of vegetation size as a measure of extracardiac disease, and the complexity of treatment decisions following transcatheter valve replacement.

title: Peri-procedural immune blood cell count changes and pacemaker implantation after transcatheter aortic valve implantation: an exploratory study.
authors: Kinga Koziarska; Anna Olasińska-Wiśniewska; Tomasz Urbanowicz; Karol Stachowiak; Jan Kaczmarek; Anna Witkowska; Bartłomiej Perek; Marek Grygier; Przemysław Mitkowski; Marek Jemielity
journal: Kardiochirurgia i torakochirurgia polska = Polish journal of cardio-thoracic surgery
abstract:
Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is a minimally invasive treatment for aortic stenosis. Although significant advancements in the TAVI technique have been made, the risk of requiring a permanent pacemaker remains clinically relevant.
The aim of the study was to analyze the relationship between peri-procedural blood count parameters and the risk of pacemaker implantation after TAVI.
The retrospective study analyzed 115 patients (median (Q1-Q3) age of 76.7 (73.5-81.9) years). Demographic and clinical data were collected. The counts of leukocytes, neutrophils, lymphocytes, monocytes, and platelets were assessed before the procedure, on the day of the procedure (8 hours after the procedure), 24, 48, and 72 hours after the procedure, and at hospital discharge. Pre-procedural and post-procedural heart rhythm disturbances have been recorded.
The analysis showed a predominant increase in neutrophil and monocyte counts after the procedure, without differences between subgroups. Moreover, a decrease in lymphocyte counts was observed after TAVI; however, it was less pronounced in patients who required pacemaker implantation. Patients without heart rhythm disturbances experienced a greater decrease in their lymphocyte count. In the multivariable analysis, an increase in lymphocyte count after the procedure was an independent factor for pacemaker implantation (OR = 5.2, 95% CI: 1.6-16.3, p = 0.005).
After TAVI, increases in neutrophil and monocyte counts and decreases in lymphocyte counts are observed; however, the lymphocyte count decrease is less pronounced in patients with heart rhythm disturbances requiring pacemaker implantation. An increase in lymphocyte count after the procedure was independently associated with pacemaker implantation.

title: Simultaneous Aortic and Mitral Valve-in-Valve Replacement Using Balloon-Expandable MyVal Valves With Bioprosthetic Valve Fracture.
authors: Nitin Bajaj; Navreet Singh; Ankush Gupta; Sunny Pathania
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
abstract: Valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve replacement and mitral valve replacement have proved to be a viable alternative to redo surgery in patients who have bioprosthetic valve dysfunction. There is a large subgroup of patients who undergo double valve replacement with bioprosthetic valves, especially in patients with rheumatic heart disease. Failure of these bioprosthetic valves would require a transcatheter management strategy. Transcatheter double valve replacement (TDVR) in these complex cases would require careful evaluation and planning of valve sizing, aortomitral interactions, access, and residual gradients. A 73-year-old man with rheumatic heart disease and prior double bioprosthetic valve replacement in 2014 presented with New York Heart Association class (NYHA) III dyspnea and exertional pre-syncope. He had severe stenosis of a 19 mm Perimount Magna aortic bioprosthesis and a 27 mm Perimount Magna mitral bioprosthesis, with pulmonary hypertension. Computed tomography demonstrated suitable anatomy for transcatheter valve-in-valve treatment. He underwent successful TDVR with a 20 mm MyVal balloon-expandable in the aortic position, followed by a post-implantation valve fracture, and a 27.5 mm MyVal transseptally in the mitral position. The final mean gradients were 15 mmHg across the aortic valve and 6 mmHg across the mitral valve at discharge. At 1-year follow-up, the patient remained clinically well without an increase in valve gradients. Simultaneous transcatheter aortic and mitral valve-in-valve replacement can be performed successfully in selected high-risk patients after meticulous multimodality planning. In patients with a small surgical aortic bioprosthesis, intentional bioprosthetic valve fracture may be an important adjunct to optimize post-implantation hemodynamics. This report highlights the complexity of procedural planning for bioprosthetic valve fracture in a small aortic valve, ensuring optimal hemodynamics and the safety and durability of the Myval transcatheter heart valve in challenging and complex procedures like TDVR.

title: Influence of diabetes mellitus on dapagliflozin response after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR): insights from the DAPA-TAVI trial.
authors: Rocío Párraga; Carlos Real; Luis Nombela-Franco; Ignacio Amat-Santos; Pilar Jimenez-Quevedo; Diego López Otero; Livia Gheorghe; Jorge Sanz-Sánchez; Carlos Baladrón Zorita; Soledad Ojeda; Rocío González Ferreiro; Antonio Jesús Muñoz García; Victoria Vilalta; Gabriela Veiga Fernández; Juan Gabriel Córdoba Soriano; Pedro Cepas-Guillén; Miriam Sandín Rollán; Xacobe Flores Ríos; Ricardo Palma-Carbajal; Roberto Martín Reyes; Rafael Romaguera; Pablo Avanzas; Sergio García Blas; Juan A Franco-Peláez; Javier Martín Moreiras; José R González-Juanatey; German Calle; José Luis Díez; Sandra Santos-Martínez; Pablo Domínguez Erquicia; Erika Muñoz García; Eduard Fernandez-Nofrerias; Xoan Sanmartín; Alejandro Gutiérrez Barrios; Inmaculada González Bermúdez; Valentín Fuster; Borja Ibáñez; Sergio Raposeiras Roubín
abstract:
The DAPA-TAVI trial demonstrated that dapagliflozin reduced the composite of all-cause mortality or worsening heart failure (HF) at 1 year in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) with prior HF. Whether the magnitude of this benefit differs according to diabetes mellitus (DM) status remains uncertain.
This pre-specified subgroup analysis of the multicenter randomized DAPA-TAVI trial conducted at 39 centers in Spain, which enrolled 1222 patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing TAVR with prior HF and at least one high-risk condition. Patients were stratified by the presence or absence of DM. The primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause mortality or worsening HF at 12 months. Secondary endpoints included the individual components of the primary endpoint, cardiovascular death, and safety outcomes. Cox proportional-hazards models adjusted for age, sex, coronary artery disease, baseline ejection fraction and baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate were used to estimate treatment effects.
Among 1222 patients, 537 (43.9%) had DM. In patients with DM, dapagliflozin significantly reduced the primary endpoint compared with standard care (15.2% vs. 22.7%; HR 0.580; 95% CI 0.389-0.866; p = 0.008; number needed to treat [NNT] = 11), driven primarily by fewer worsening HF events. In patients without DM, the reduction was numerically lower and non-significant (15.0% vs. 18.0%; HR 0.814; 95% CI 0.560-1.183; p = 0.280; NNT = 32). Genital infections were more frequent with dapagliflozin in patients with DM, whereas symptomatic hypotension was more common in those without DM. No significant differences in serious adverse events were observed in either subgroup. No statistically significant interactions between DM status and treatment effect were observed for the primary or secondary endpoints.
In this pre-specified subanalysis of the DAPA-TAVI trial, dapagliflozin significantly reduced the risk of death or worsening HF in patients with DM undergoing TAVR, with a favorable benefit-risk profile, whereas a more modest and non-significant effect was observed in non-DM patients. Although no statistically significant interaction according to diabetes status was observed, the apparently greater benefit among patients with DM warrants further investigation.

title: Incomplete Shone's complex as a rare cardiac manifestation of Coffin-Lowry syndrome: a case report.
authors: Gytė Gužauskaitė; Skaistė Sendžikaitė; Birutė Burnytė
abstract:
Coffin-Lowry syndrome is a rare X-linked genetic disorder caused by pathogenic variants in the RPS6KA3 gene, characterized by distinctive craniofacial features, skeletal abnormalities, and neurodevelopmental impairment. Although cardiac involvement has been reported in Coffin-Lowry syndrome, it most commonly manifests as cardiomyopathy or valvular insufficiency. To the best of our knowledge, Coffin-Lowry syndrome has not been associated with obstructive left-sided congenital heart diseases including an incomplete Shone's complex.
We report a case of a 2-month-old boy who, on cardiac evaluation, was found to have coarctation of the aorta, a bicuspid aortic valve with severe stenosis, a parachute-like mitral valve with mild subvalvular stenosis, consistent with an incomplete Shone's complex, and marked left ventricular hypertrophy. The patient underwent successful corrective surgery for coarctation of the aorta and aortic valve stenosis, with follow-up revealing moderate residual aortic valve stenosis and mild residual valvular dysfunction. Genetic testing identified a maternally inherited microduplication of the X chromosome p22.12 region, encompassing several 5' exons of the RPS6KA3 gene.
This case suggests that obstructive left-sided congenital heart diseases including an incomplete Shone's complex may represent a previously unrecognized cardiac manifestations of Coffin-Lowry syndrome, thereby expanding the cardiovascular phenotype of this rare condition. Recognition of this association may have implications for early diagnosis, genetic evaluation, and long-term cardiac surveillance in affected patients.

title: Moderate aortic stenosis identified during intensive care admission for a non-cardiac primary diagnosis and 90-day mortality: a retrospective cohort study using the MIMIC-IV echocardiography database.
authors: Lujun Shao; Cheng Xu; Huiyu Tai; Yue Li
abstract:
Moderate aortic stenosis is associated with reduced survival in ambulatory cardiology populations, but its prognostic significance when identified during an intensive care admission for a non-cardiac primary diagnosis is unknown. We examined its association with 90-day mortality in this setting.
Retrospective cohort using the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) version 3.1 and its echocardiogram-matched subset (MIMIC-IV-ECHO). We included each adult's first intensive care admission for a non-cardiac primary diagnosis with an interpretable baseline transthoracic echocardiogram recording peak aortic jet velocity. Stenosis was graded from the peak velocity (no stenosis < 2.0, sclerosis or mild 2.0-2.9, moderate 3.0-3.9, severe ≥ 4.0 m/s). The echocardiogram defined time zero; the primary outcome was all-cause mortality within a fixed 90-day window. Associations were estimated with multivariable Cox models adjusted for acute-illness severity and comorbidity, with propensity-score matching, velocity-gradient concordance grading, pre-specified ejection-fraction subgroups, and an E-value.
Of 12,878 patients (10,511 no stenosis, 1,797 sclerosis, 411 moderate, 159 severe), 3,605 died within 90 days. Crude 90-day mortality rose across grades (26.1%, 34.4%, 40.4%, 46.5%). After adjustment, the hazard increased monotonically: sclerosis 1.17 (95% CI 1.07-1.28), moderate 1.33 (1.13-1.56), severe 1.61 (1.27-2.03). The moderate-stenosis association was modest but consistent, attenuating slightly in the most conservative specifications (propensity-score matched 1.20 [1.02-1.40]; parsimonious 1.22 [1.05-1.43]); the E-value was 1.73 (lower limit 1.41). It was numerically concentrated in the first two weeks (1.58 [1.30-1.93], days 0-14) and numerically larger with reduced (1.47 [1.10-1.97]) than preserved ejection fraction (1.10 [0.87-1.39]); neither the proportional-hazards nor the grade-by-ejection-fraction interaction test was significant (interaction P = 0.21), and both are exploratory numerical patterns, not demonstrated effect modification.
In non-cardiac critical illness, velocity-defined moderate aortic stenosis identified during the intensive care admission was independently associated with higher 90-day mortality, with exploratory numerical patterns of greater early risk and of greater risk with reduced ejection fraction. These data identify a higher-risk phenotype; they do not establish a causal adverse effect of moderate valvular obstruction itself. It is best regarded as a prognostic marker warranting closer surveillance rather than, on current evidence, a target for valve intervention.

title: Bicuspid Aortic Stenosis: Is it Time to Refine Our Classification Before We Randomize?
authors: Karl Poon; Syed Zaid; Gilbert H L Tang

title: Development of a Quantitative Contrast CT-Based TAVR-Risk Score to Reliably Predict Deformation in Bicuspid Aortic Valves.
authors: Kazuki Suruga; Vivek Patel; Hasan Jilaihawi; Hidemasa Shitan; Tej Sheth; Yuchao Guo; Takashi Nagasaka; Daniel Ng; Tarun Chakravarty; Wen Cheng; Yuito Okada; Aakriti Gupta; Mamoo Nakamura; Raj R Makkar
abstract:
Bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) calcification affects clinical outcomes by causing transcatheter heart valve (THV) deformation after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). However, a computed tomography (CT)-based scoring system for grading BAV calcification severity and predicting THV deformation has not been established.
This study sought to develop a cardiac CT-based BAV TAVR-risk score for grading BAV calcification severity and predicting THV deformation.
This single-center retrospective study included consecutive patients with BAV who underwent TAVR using contemporary balloon-expandable valves between January 2016 and December 2024 and who had preprocedural and postprocedural CT imaging. The BAV TAVR-risk score integrated calcification severity and distribution across valve leaflets, raphe, annulus, and left ventricular outflow tract, quantified using a fixed HU-850 threshold of detection on contrast-enhanced CT scans. Score thresholds were derived by receiver operating curve analysis with Youden index optimization. Patients were categorized into low-, intermediate-, and high-risk score groups.
Among 321 patients (median follow-up: 1,825 days; Q1-Q3: 765-1,825 days), 56 (17.4%) were classified into the high-risk score group. Both underexpansion and eccentricity of the THV occurred in 49 of the 321 patients (15.3%) and were predominantly observed in the high-risk score group. However, in the low-risk score group, 149 of 155 patients (96.1%) demonstrated no underexpansion or eccentricity of the THV. A high BAV TAVR-risk score independently predicted both underexpansion and eccentricity of the THV (OR: 89.13; 95% CI: 35.02-226.83; P < 0.001).
This CT-based BAV TAVR-risk score provides a systematic method to precisely quantify BAV severity which reliably predicts THV deformation for BAV patients with contemporary balloon-expandable valves and may help guide decision-making in this challenging population.

title: Transcatheter vs Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement for Isolated Native Aortic Regurgitation: National Propensity-Matched Analysis.
authors: Yukari Kobayashi; Afek Kodesh; Maria C Alu; Alexandra Popma; David J Cohen; Martin B Leon; Juan F Granada; Jeffrey J Popma; Harun Kundi
abstract:
Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is well established for aortic stenosis, while its application for isolated native aortic regurgitation (AR) was previously off label and technically challenging. Comparative data between TAVR and surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) are limited.
The aim of this study was to compare patient characteristics and outcomes of off-label TAVR vs SAVR among patients with isolated native AR.
Using the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services Medicare Provider Analysis and Review database, patients ≥65 years of age who underwent TAVR or SAVR for isolated native AR (2017-2023) were identified. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed to evaluate short- and long-term outcomes. Fine-Gray models accounted for death as a competing risk, reported as subdistribution HRs (SHRs).
Among 9,859 patients, 1,742 propensity score-matched pairs were included, with balanced baseline characteristics (mean age 75.8 years vs 75.7 years; female sex 517 of 1,742 [29.7%] vs 528 of 1,742 [30.3%]). In the matched cohort, TAVR was associated with shorter hospitalization (OR: 0.33; 95% CI: 0.28-0.39; P < 0.001) and lower in-hospital mortality (OR: 0.62; 95% CI: 0.39-1.00; P = 0.048) but higher 30-day pacemaker implantation (OR: 1.73; 95% CI: 1.33-2.25; P < 0.001). Through 5 years (median follow-up 2.58 years), TAVR was associated with increased repeat aortic valve replacement (SHR: 2.04; 95% CI: 1.13-3.66) but similar all-cause mortality (HR: 1.14; 95% CI: 0.98-1.31) and heart failure-related readmission (SHR: 1.09; 95% CI: 0.98-1.21) between treatment strategies.
In this analysis, TAVR was associated with shorter hospitalization and comparable 5-year survival as SAVR, although pacemaker and long-term reinterventions rates were higher.

title: Paravalvular Regurgitation After TAVR in Low-Flow, Low-Gradient Aortic Stenosis: How Much Is Too Much?
authors: George D Dangas; Angelo Oliva

title: Prognostic Impact of Paravalvular Regurgitation in Patients With Severe Low-Flow, Low-Gradient Aortic Stenosis Undergoing TAVR.
authors: Michele Bellino; Angelo Silverio; Germano Junior Ferruzzi; Francesco Saia; Antonio Giulio Bruno; Paride Boragine; Andrea Buono; Maria Luisa De Rosa; Francesco Paolo Cancro; Italo Porto; Gabriele Crimi; Paolo Calabrò; Elisabetta Moscarella; Alfonso Ielasi; Carolina Montonati; Marco De Carlo; Alessandro Sticchi; Francesca Lanni; Luca Esposito; Francesca Maria Di Muro; Francesco Maiellaro; Ivan Francesco Calchera; Giacomo Boccuzzi; Antonio Sorropago; Fernando Scudiero; Tiziana Attisano; Rodolfo Citro; Giovanni Granata; Giuseppe De Luca; Carmine Vecchione; Giuseppe Musumeci; Gennaro Galasso; LOW-TAVR Investigators
abstract:
Paravalvular regurgitation (PVR) is a frequent complication after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) and may influence clinical outcomes in patients with high-gradient aortic stenosis. However, its prognostic relevance in patients with low-flow, low-gradient aortic stenosis (LFLG-AS) undergoing TAVR remains incompletely elucidated.
This study sought to evaluate the prognostic significance of PVR severity in patients with LFLG-AS undergoing TAVR with current-generation prostheses.
This multicenter registry-based cohort study included consecutive patients with LFLG-AS undergoing TAVR from January 2019 to December 2024 at 17 high-volume Italian centers. PVR severity was classified using a 5-class grading scheme and stratified as <2+ (none/trace or mild) or ≥2+ (mild-moderate or worse) based on separation of Kaplan-Meier curves for the primary outcome. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause death and heart failure hospitalization up to 2 years. Propensity score-weighted Cox regression was used to estimate the independent impact of PVR severity on clinical outcomes.
A total of 1,358 patients were included. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed lower event-free survival among patients with ≥2+ PVR at discharge compared with those with <2+ PVR. After propensity score weighting, PVR ≥2+ was independently associated with a higher risk of the primary endpoint (adjusted HR: 3.77; 95% CI: 2.88-4.95), as well as higher risks of all-cause death, mainly cardiovascular, and heart failure hospitalization. These findings were consistent across both classical and paradoxical LFLG-AS phenotypes.
In this large, real-world study of patients with LFLG-AS treated with current-generation TAVR devices, PVR ≥2+ was independently associated with worse clinical outcomes after discharge, regardless of LFLG-AS subtype.

title: Prevalence and Consequences of Guideline-Directed Indications for Aortic Valve Replacement in the EARLY TAVR Trial.
authors: Mahesh V Madhavan; Allan Schwartz; Brian R Lindman; Philippe Pibarot; David J Cohen; J Bradley Oldemeyer; Vasilis Babaliaros; William F Fearon; David Daniels; Adnan Chhatriwalla; Clifford J Kavinsky; Pinak Shah; Molly Szerlip; Thom Dahle; Kashish Goel; William O'Neill; Raj Makkar; Charles Davidson; Tej Sheth; Paul Sorajja; James DeVries; Jeffrey Southard; Jeremiah P Depta; Andrei Pop; Rebbecca T Hahn; Yanglu Zhao; Martin B Leon; Philippe Genereux; EARLY TAVR Trial Executive Committee and Study Investigators
abstract:
The current American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association valvular heart disease guidelines were published before several recent trials that provide greater support for early intervention in patients with asymptomatic severe aortic stenosis (AS).
This study sought to investigate the prevalence and clinical impact of American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Class II recommendations for AVR in the EARLY TAVR trial.
The EARLY TAVR trial randomized patients with asymptomatic severe AS to transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) with a balloon-expandable valve or clinical surveillance (CS) with conversion to TAVR based on development of ACC/AHA Class I indications. Patients in the intention-to-treat cohort were stratified by presence of a Class II indication for AVR at randomization. The primary endpoint of the present analysis was the composite of all-cause death, stroke, or heart failure hospitalization. Interaction tests were performed to assess whether the treatment effect differed by level of guideline recommendation. Timing of conversion to AVR in the CS group according to the presence/absence of Class II indications was also assessed.
Of the 901 patients randomized to TAVR (N = 445) and CS (N = 446), 636 (70.6%) patients had no guideline recommendation, and 265 (29.4%) had at least1 1 Class II recommendation for AVR at the time of randomization. At a median follow-up of 3.8 years, patients with a Class II indication for AVR experienced higher rates of the primary endpoint (Class II: 24.5% vs no recommendation: 14.5%; HR = 1.78; 95% CI: 1.30-2.44; P < 0.001) and were more likely to have acute valve syndrome at the time of conversion. Compared with CS, the relative benefit of early TAVR on the primary endpoint was similar regardless of the presence or absence of a Class II guideline recommendation (HR = 0.62; 95% CI: 0.37-1.02 vs 0.61; 95% CI: 0.40-0.92; Pinteraction = 0.96).
Among patients in the EARLY TAVR trial, Class II indications for AVR were present in almost one-third of patients at baseline. The benefit of early TAVR was consistent regardless of the presence or absence of Class II indications. These findings support the strategy of early TAVR over CS in asymptomatic patients with severe AS, independent of guideline indications.

abstract: Introduction: Height, weight, and age of person has significant impact on the normal size of heart. These parameters need to be considered when cut-off values indicating the need for treatment or even surgery are established. The aim of present work is to study the relation of weight of the heart with age and weight of cadaver. Material and Methods: The study was performed in the Department of Anatomy, Shri Ram Murti Smarak Institute of Medical Sciences, Bareilly on 30 hearts from embalmed cadavers. The hearts were procured from the cadavers available in our department. The heart was thoroughly cleaned and measurements were taken. Results: The mean heart weight was 223.37 ± 57.78 g. Significant relationship between age of the cadaver and weight of the heart (p=0.0004), weight of cadaver and weight of heart (p=0.0001) was observed. Conclusion: The above study provides valuable data of the heart in our geographical location, which may be useful for cardiac surgeons and physicians.

title: Understanding pedagogical challenges faced by technology teachers in special needs classrooms
authors: Katane Elizabeth Kekana; Thokozani Isaac Mtshali
journal: Journal of Education and Learning Technology
abstract: Teaching learners with special educational needs requires dynamic and adaptive pedagogical strategies that can lead to social development and academic success. This can be possible if teachers are assisted in mitigating the daily challenges of teaching such learners. This qualitative exploratory case study investigated the pedagogical challenges encountered by two Grade 9 Technology teachers in the Capricorn District of Limpopo Province. This study used Shulman’s Content and Pedagogical Knowledge framework to understand teachers’ challenges. Data was collected through semi-structured interviews and classroom observations; all collected data were analysed thematically. This study found that teachers experienced various challenges, including the emotional labour of teaching, burnout in the LSEN environment and the enactment of instructional knowledge. The study concluded that the sampled teachers displayed weaknesses in lesson planning, activating learners’ prior knowledge, diagnosing errors, achieving curriculum objectives and sustaining engagement. As a result, it was recommended that support through teacher assistants, creative differentiated strategies and enhanced digital-technology literacy to improve outcomes for learners with special needs was imminent.

title: Integration of Biomechanics and Digital Technology: Using Kinovea for Motion Analysis and Learning for Beginner Athletes
authors: Muhammad Nur Hudha; Riezky Maya Probosari; Annisa Nur Khasanah; Supurwoko; Salsabila Kholifahtun Nisa’; Gifran Rihla Gifarka Latief
journal: Journal of Coaching and Sports Science
abstract: Background: The integration of biomechanics with digital motion-analysis technologies has introduced new approaches for examining movement efficiency, kinematic characteristics, and technical patterns in walking and running activities. Kinovea, as an accessible motion-analysis software, provides both visual and quantitative feedback. However, its application in supporting technique development among beginner athletes remains insufficiently explored. Aim: This study aims to describe the use of Kinovea in biomechanics training and examine its contribution to the awareness of kinematic characteristics and movement techniques among beginner athletes. Methods: A descriptive qualitative design involved 72 beginner athletes aged 18–25 years selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected over 16 weeks through interviews, field observations, and motion video recordings analyzed using Kinovea. Kinematic data focused on joint angles, stride behavior, and movement phases during walking, running, and the flight phase. Qualitative data were analyzed using content analysis with NVivo 12, while kinematic results were interpreted descriptively to identify performance patterns and areas for technical refinement. Result: Kinematic analysis showed coordinated joint-angle patterns across all phases. Walking analysis identified arm swing angles of 50.9°–58.8° and leg separation angles of 64.3°–67.2°, indicating a stable gait rhythm. The running analysis revealed knee angles of 68.8°–69.8° and elbow angles of 87.6°–89.1°, indicating efficient propulsive mechanics. The flight phase demonstrated knee angles of 81.2°–87.8° and elbow angles of 80.4°–88.3°, suggesting effective momentum use and postural stability. These measurements supported stride-efficiency assessment and technique evaluation. Qualitative findings revealed that Kinovea enabled athletes to interpret movement phases and identify technical inefficiencies through slow-motion and frame-by-frame visualization. Conclusion: Kinovea supports basic motion analysis by providing clear kinematic information and helping beginner athletes observe and refine their movement techniques. The findings also offer practical value for coaches by enabling more precise identification of inefficient patterns and guiding targeted corrections during early-stage training.

title: A Review of Phishing Detection Techniques Using Machine Learning and Natural Language Processing
authors: Dr. Sunita Dixit
journal: Journal of Global Research in Multidisciplinary Studies(JGRMS)
abstract: The goal of phishing attacks, which rank high among cyber risks, is to steal sensitive information (such as login passwords, financial data, and more) from unsuspecting people and companies. Blacklist, whitelist, rule, heuristic, and signature-based detection methods are no longer suitable due to the rising sophistication of phishing schemes. As a result, ML, DL, and NLP are rapidly becoming into effective instruments for detecting both well-known and brand-new forms of phishing. Background on phishing assaults, old ways of detecting them, and recent advances in intelligent phishing detection are all included in this article. It delves into several machine learning algorithms such as decision tree, LSTM, ANN, CNN, and RNN, as well as deep learning models like KNN, NB, and SVM. Also, natural language processing methods including word embedding, sentiment analysis, text categorization, and tokenization are explored with the aim of detecting phishing material. Presenting a comprehensive, precise, and up-to-the-minute phishing detection system is the ultimate goal of this study, which focuses on machine learning frameworks, performance indicators, present obstacles, and future research directions.

journal: Научный журнал "Вестник Актюбинского регионального университета имени К. Жубанова"
abstract: In the context of increasing complexity of modern network infrastructures and the growing number of cyberattacks, improving the effectiveness of intrusion detection systems is a highly relevant task. The aim of this work is to develop and investigate a hybrid approach to network attack detection based on a combination of signature-based analysis and intelligent machine learning methods.  The research methods include analysis of requirements for anomaly detection systems, comparative analysis of existing solutions, design of a hybrid system architecture, and experimental modeling using multiclass classification of network traffic. The results demonstrate that integrating a neural model with a traditional detection system improves attack detection coverage and reduces the number of false positives.  The practical significance of the study lies in the possibility of deploying the proposed architecture in real corporate networks, while the theoretical significance consists in substantiating the effectiveness of a hybrid approach to traffic analysis. Future research directions include adaptive model training and expansion of the range of detectable attacks.
